question.leadin: Answer the following about Aaron Burr, (sir).
question.text: In his later life, Aaron Burr was involved in a bizarre plan to establish himself as the hereditary emperor of this country, America's southern neighbor.
question.clue: The Plan of Ayala was proclaimed by a revolutionary whose base of power in this country was the state of Morelos.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about people in the "Leaders" section of the 2017 TIME 100.
swap.text: This man won the 2016 Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to make peace with rebel groups in Colombia, including FARC.

question.leadin: In a 19th century civil war in this country, Fructuoso Rivera's Colorados fought Manuel Oribe's agrarian Blancos.
question.text: Name this South American country where wealthy businessmen in Montevideo [mon-tay-vih-DAY-oh] supported the Colorados, the eventual winning side.
question.clue: The Italian Legion was raised in this country by the "Hero of Two Worlds," who fought in this country's civil war with the Colorados against the Blancos.

swap.leadin: Former secretary of state John Kerry claimed that this country was a "narco-kleptocracy."
swap.text: Name this Central American country once led by Manuel Noriega that separated from Colombia in 1903. It was invaded by the United States in Operation Just Cause in 1989.
swap.clue: Operation Nifty Package sunk the boat of a leader of this country, who subsequently hid in its Vatican diplomatic mission.

question.leadin: This leader founded the 26th of July Movement after launching an attack on the Moncada Barracks.
question.text: Name this revolutionary leader who overthrew Fulgencio Batista. In his position as Prime Minister, he allowed the Soviet Union to place MRBMs in his country.
question.clue: Che Guevara joined this man's 26th of July Movement.

swap.text: Bolivar met with this Argentinian General at Guayaquil ["Gway-ah-keel"], Ecuador. This man led the Army of the Andes to a victory in the Battle of Chacabuco.
swap.answerHtml: Jose de San Martin [or José Francisco de San Martín y Matorras]
swap.clue: This leader defeated Manuel Osorio alongside Bernardo O'Higgins at Maipu after winning at Chacabuco.

question.leadin: This man's intelligence service was run by Vladimiro Montesinos, who requested that ten thousand AK-47s be air-dropped to troops fighting against Abimael Guzman.
question.text: Name this man of Japanese descent, who incurred many human rights violations for campaigns against the Shinng Path guerrillas during his ten-year rule.
question.answerHtml: Alberto Fujimori [fun fact: in Spanish, the "j" in this name is pronounced like an English "h"]
question.clue: A paramilitary group supporting this leader, Grupo Colina, killed fifteen partygoers in the Barrios Altos massacre.

swap.leadin: In the 1500s the demand and economy of silver grew.
swap.text: Name this Spanish legal system, practiced before the hacienda, which entrusted authority and land to colonists who would ideally protect Indians and convert them to Roman Catholics, while extracting precious silver and gold from them.
swap.clue: Despite the fact that religious orders retained control over all lands under its jurisdiction, reformers like Bartolome de las Casas sought to eliminate all systems under which natives were assimilated.

question.text: While the details for a trade agreement were hammered out in February, the final signing of trade pact between the United States and this country was delayed until June 6 because of President Ricardo Lagos's opposition to the Iraqi war. For 15 points-name this South American country.
question.clue: After its neighbor imposed a ten cent tax on this country's saltpeter production, this country seized the city of Antofagasta and triggered a war which landlocked that neighbor.

swap.text: Though he was badly beaten at Rancagua, this governor of Concepcion (kun sepp see ON) escaped and returned to fight, ultimately deefating the royalists at Chacabuco. For 15 points, name this revolutionary leader who became the first Chilean head of state in 1817.
swap.clue: After he was deposed by Ramon Freire, this man was offered the post of governor of Concepcion, though he declined and moved to the Cuiva and Montalvan plantations.

question.leadin: The "Day of the Sea" in Bolivia commemorates its loss of its coastline in this war.
question.text: Name this war which was lost by a Bolivian-Peruvian alliance, ending with the Treaty of Ancon. An alternative name for this war comes from a resource used as fertilizer, on which Bolivia attempted to raise taxes.
question.answerHtml: War of the Pacific [or Guerra del Pacifico; accept Saltpeter War or Nitrate War or Ten Cents War or Second Pacific War or Guerra del Salitre; reject “Guano War”]
question.clue: One cause of this war was a ten-centavo tax on saltpeter, and Peru tried to mediate talks between the two sides before it joined the war itself.

swap.leadin: This city was the capital of the Portuguese Empire from 1808 to 1821.
swap.text: Name this capital of Brazil until it was moved to Brasilia. This city hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics.
swap.clue: The large slum of Rocinha was built on a hill in this city.

question.leadin: A group named for this man led a guerrilla campaign that overthrew the military regime of Anastasio Somoza.
question.text: Name this man who was killed by the National Guard of Anastasio Somoza. The group named after this man was led by Daniel Ortega and fought against the Contras.
question.clue: At the end of his country's Constitutionalist War, this general refused to lay down his arms and instead waged a guerrilla war against the U.S. Marines occupying his country.

swap.leadin: He only served officially as President of his country from 1930-38 and 1942-52 during his thirty one year rule.
swap.text: Identify this Caribbean dictator that seized control from Horacio Vasquez in a military coup in 1930 and whose political opponents included Juan Bosch.
swap.clue: This dictator took power by overthrowing Horacio Vasquez, used pancake makeup to make himself appear whiter, and unsuccessfully attempted to blow up Venezuelan president Romulo Betancourt.

question.leadin: After its independence from Spain, this country was led by Jose Gaspar Rodriguez de Francia, the basis for Augusto Roa Bastos's Yo el Supremo.
question.text: Name this South American country which fought against the Triple Alliance in the 1860s and has its capital at Asuncion.
question.clue: A 19th century leader of this country established a secret police called the pyragues, or hairy-feet, that would be re-established in the 1960s. This country entered a prolonged military buildup under its presidents, Carlos Lopez and Gaspar de Francia.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about a revolution.
swap.text: Published in 1938 by the Trinidadian writer C.L.R. James, this book was the first history of the Haitian Revolution told from the perspective of the revolutionaries.
swap.clue: This history of the Haitian Revolution written by C.L.R. James linked the Haitian struggle with the French Revolution and its ideals.

question.text: The largest quilombo was this community in the state of Alagoas. This community was also known as Angola Janga and was led by Ganga Zamba and later by Zumbi, whose head was put on display in Recife.
question.clue: Residents of this place called each other malungo, meaning "comrade."

swap.text: De Anza started his journey from one of these fortified Spanish military settlements in Sonora. De Anza also laid the foundation for a location with this name in San Francisco that was converted into an American military post.
swap.clue: This imperial outposts that included the Penon, La Goletta, and Melilla ("may-LEE-yuh"). Philip II retained a state of five ports named for these buildings after the Medici conquered Siena.

question.leadin: This president's final re-election campaign used a jingle themed around the slogan "lo hizo," meaning that "he did" things like signing the Buenos Aires Act.
question.text: Name this Federal Peronist president during whose term Alfredo Yabran killed himself after ordering a hit on journalist Jose Luis Cabezas. This Syrian-Argentine president of the 1990s illegally sold arms to Croatia.
question.clue: Elected president of Argentina in 1989, this man was the first Peronist to be elected president since 1973. He was the first Argentine president to visit Great Britain since the Falkland War and was succeeded by Fernando de la Rua.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about two historically opposed groups from Latin America, FTPE.
swap.text: Founded in opposition to Manuel Oribe, this liberal reformist party catered to the interests of urban Montevideo and was got its name from the blue, and later red, armbands worn by its members.
swap.clue: This party, once led by Jose Batlle (BAT-zhay), controlled a capital city that was besieged by Manuel Oribe for nine years during a civil war called the "Guerra Grande."
